original_question: A finite group G is said to be semi-abelian if it has a sequence of subgroups 1 = G0 ⩽ G1 ⩽ · · · ⩽ Gn = G such that for every i the subgroup Gi+1 is isomorphic to a quotient of a semidirect product Ai ⋊ Gi for some abelian group Ai. Conjecture: Semi-abelian finite groups are monomial.
target_in_paper: Problem 21.68 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)": whether every finite semi-abelian group is monomial. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, you should define "monomial": a finite group is monomial if each irreducible character of it is induced from a linear character of some subgroup. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

If one wants standard character-theoretic precision beyond the notebook’s shorthand, one may say "irreducible complex character"; the paper itself simply says "irreducible character." ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
refined_question: Let G be a finite group. Call G semi-abelian if there exists a chain of subgroups 1 = G0 ≤ G1 ≤ ··· ≤ Gn = G such that for each i = 0, 1, ..., n − 1, the subgroup Gi+1 is isomorphic to a quotient of a semidirect product Ai ⋊ Gi for some abelian group Ai. Must every such G be monomial; that is, must every irreducible character of G be induced from a linear character of some subgroup of G? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
